title: Fix: dpkg was interrupted, you must manually run dpkg --configure -a
summary: Apt stops with 'dpkg was interrupted' when an earlier install or update was cut off before it finished. Finishing the interrupted setup and then repairing broken dependencies usually fixes it.

aliases.text: dpkg was interrupted you must manually run dpkg configure -a
dpkg прерван, нужно вручную выполнить dpkg --configure -a

error_patterns: dpkg was interrupted, you must manually run
prerequisites: The error appeared in a terminal after apt or apt-get was run, and no install or update is still running

steps.explain: Check which packages are left half-installed. This only reads the package database and changes nothing.
steps.expect: Empty output means no package is broken. If packages are listed under 'only half configured', continue with the next step.

steps.explain: Finish setting up every package that the interrupted install left half-configured.
steps.expect: Lines like 'Setting up <package> ...' appear and the prompt returns with no error.

steps.explain: Install missing dependencies and repair packages whose dependencies are broken.
steps.expect: Ends with a line like '0 upgraded, 0 newly installed' or a list of packages to install. If apt asks 'Do you want to continue?', type y and press Enter.

steps.explain: Refresh the list of available packages so apt works from current information. This does not install or upgrade anything.
steps.expect: Lines starting with 'Hit:' or 'Get:' appear, then 'Reading package lists...'. A message about upgradable packages is normal.

verify.expect: No output. Nothing is left half-installed, and the command exits without errors.

rollback.explain: Nothing here is undone automatically. The packages that were set up in the steps stay installed. To remove one you do not want, use 'sudo apt remove <PACKAGE>' with the package name shown by the earlier output.

warnings: Do not delete /var/lib/dpkg/lock or the files in /var/lib/dpkg/updates by hand. This can damage the package database.
Do not turn off the computer or close the terminal while dpkg or apt is running.
If the same error comes back, run 'dpkg --audit' again and note the package names it lists before trying anything else.

source.title: dpkg manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
